answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the value it handles, like a crystal forming layer by layer: cheap to start, expensive to fake at scale. Newcomers begin in a shared grove of low-trust tasks, earning reputation only through verified work that peers attest. When the tide of new identities surges, the stake and the slow reputation ramp make mass forgery unprofitable, because an attacker must fund and age thousands of accounts before any of them can touch high-value work.
